title: Army-CJNG Clash in Jilotlán de los Dolores, Jalisco Leaves 4 Suspected Gunmen and a Soldier Dead
detail: On September 13, 2026, Mexican Army Special Forces, National Guard, the FGR, and three Mexican Air Force helicopters raided two suspected CJNG narco-camps in the municipality of Jilotlán de los Dolores, southern Jalisco. Personnel came under gunfire while clearing the camps; in the exchange, four suspected gunmen were killed. Two soldiers were wounded and evacuated by helicopter to the Military Hospital in Apatzingán, Michoacán, where one later died, bringing the operation's total death toll to five. Seized items included a .50-caliber Barrett rifle, four additional long guns, roughly 138 improvised explosive devices, ammunition, tactical clothing, and six vehicles (one factory-armored). In a related same-day operation in Santa María del Oro, authorities separately dismantled a clandestine methamphetamine lab, seizing industrial reactors and condensers, over 1,600 liters of precursor chemicals, 1,140 kg of ammonia powder, and 150 kg of calcium chloride.

confidenceReason: The clash, casualties, and seized items are corroborated by multiple independent Tier-2 Mexican outlets citing federal security sources (Army, National Guard, FGR); the suspects' formal CJNG affiliation is the outlets' attribution pending judicial confirmation.

title: Alleged CJNG Collaborator 'El Neto' Arrested in Tijuana, Linked to Killing of Baja California State Police Officer
detail: On September 13, 2026, agents of Baja California's Fuerza Estatal de Seguridad Ciudadana (FESC) captured José Ernesto 'N,' 32, alias 'El Neto' or 'El Gordo,' in the Pedregal de Santa Julia neighborhood of Tijuana during a routine patrol. When the suspect noticed the patrol on Pintores Street he attempted to flee, discarding a Taurus 9mm pistol loaded with 11 cartridges before being apprehended. Authorities identified him as an alleged CJNG collaborator and a priority target linked to the homicide of an officer of Baja California's Secretaría de Seguridad Ciudadana, as well as suspected arms trafficking. He was transferred to the Fiscalía General de la República (FGR), which will determine his legal status.

confidenceReason: The arrest, seized firearm, and officer-homicide linkage are confirmed by Baja California's state security force and corroborated by two independent Tier-2 outlets; the suspect's formal CJNG affiliation is the outlets' attribution pending judicial confirmation.
